desc:
A string of length n has 2n - 1 possible palindrome centers: the n characters themselves and the n - 1 gaps between neighbouring characters. Number them 0 .. 2n - 2 from left to right, so center 2i is the character s[i] and center 2i + 1 is the gap between s[i] and s[i+1].

Return an array of length 2n - 1 whose entry c is the length of the longest palindromic substring centered exactly at center c. For a character center the length is at least 1; for a gap center it is 0 when the two neighbours differ.

Example: for s = "abba" the answer is [1, 0, 1, 4, 1, 0, 1]; the gap between the two b characters is the center of the whole string, a palindrome of length 4.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: Expanding outwards from every center works and is O(n²) in the worst case (for example on a string of one repeated letter). Which work is repeated?
Insert a separator such as # between all characters (and at both ends) so that odd and even palindromes become one kind: palindromes of the new string centered at each position.

Maintain the palindrome that reaches furthest to the right (center c, right edge r). For a new center i < r, its mirror 2c - i already knows a radius that can be copied, capped by r - i; only extend by direct comparison beyond that.
editorial: This is Manacher's algorithm. Transform s into t = #s0#s1#...# of length 2n + 1. A palindrome of s centered at a character or a gap corresponds to a palindrome of t centered at a position of t, and its radius in t equals its length in s. So we need rad[i], the largest r with t[i-r..i+r] a palindrome.

Keep the rightmost-reaching palindrome [c - rad[c], c + rad[c]]. For a new center i inside it, the mirror position 2c - i has the same palindromic surroundings as long as we stay inside the big palindrome, so rad[i] starts at min(rad[2c - i], c + rad[c] - i). Then try to extend by comparing characters; each successful comparison pushes the right edge further, and the right edge only moves forward.

That amortised argument gives O(n) total time and O(n) space. The entries for t positions 1 .. 2n - 1 are exactly the requested array (position 1 is the character s[0], position 2 the first gap, and so on).
solution:
def palindromeLengths(s):
    n = len(s)
    t = '#' + '#'.join(s) + '#'
    m = len(t)
    rad = [0] * m
    c = r = 0
    for i in range(m):
        if i < r:
            rad[i] = min(r - i, rad[2 * c - i])
        a, b = i + rad[i] + 1, i - rad[i] - 1
        while b >= 0 and a < m and t[a] == t[b]:
            rad[i] += 1
            a += 1
            b -= 1
        if i + rad[i] > r:
            c, r = i, i + rad[i]
    return rad[1:m - 1]
